name: Body fat
rangeNote: These published comparison ranges depend on age and sex (Gallagher 2000): men 8–20 % at 20–39 years, 11–22 % at 40–59, 13–25 % at 60–79; women 21–33 %, 23–34 % and 24–36 %. They were inferred from BMI categories, not validated as minimum and maximum healthy body-fat levels. Being outside them alone does not establish a health problem. No age-specific comparison is given under 20 or from 80. The study used lab methods (DXA and similar); home impedance scales can vary with hydration, so compare readings taken the same way.
summary: The share of your weight that is fat. It says more than weight alone, but home measurements are rough estimates: follow the trend rather than a single number.

high.meaning: More body fat for your age and sex is linked to higher heart and metabolic risk, especially fat around the belly.

low.meaning: Very low body fat can upset hormones and, in women, periods. It is uncommon outside athletes and illness.

sources.title: Healthy percentage body fat ranges: an approach for developing guidelines based on body mass index
